input: The recommendation under consideration is to install the scheduling system at Plant 2 first and hold the other plants until Plant 2 results are reported. The operations director owns the scheduling programme. The firm runs 4 plants, with revenue of $115 million per year. The evidence base is order records for 12 months, covering 12793 orders. On-time delivery over the last two quarters was 84%, against a target of 95%. Plant 2 accounts for 68% of late orders. The order backlog stands at 3.6 weeks, against 1.6 weeks a year ago. Overtime cost was $1.7 million last year, up 18% on the year before. Late orders, overtime, and backlog have all moved the wrong way together, and the late orders are concentrated in a single plant. A scheduling system for all plants is quoted at $273k; Plant 2 alone is $111k. An internal estimate puts the overtime reduction at Plant 2 at 15–20% in the first year; the estimate is internal, not a vendor figure. The phased route commits $111k and leaves the all-plants decision to the reported Plant 2 result. The other plants take the system only if the Plant 2 result supports the internal estimate in full.
